principle: treat the Moreyra Japanese target-capture samples as a reusable public skeleton; fill empty species slots and repair weak Japanese tips before collecting redundant new duplicates of already adequate public anchors

hole_classes.placement: two wild Japanese individuals, preferably from different populations or separated occurrences; exact branch placement is an inference from target capture and must not be assumed before sequencing
hole_classes.claim: fills a missing species tip in the nationwide scaffold

hole_classes.placement: replace the primary Japanese representation with two voucher-linked wild Japanese individuals; retain the old public accession only as a labelled sensitivity sample when appropriate
hole_classes.claim: repairs provenance or identity rather than adding a new species

hole_classes.placement: keep the adequate Moreyra accession as one species-tree representative and add one new wild Japanese voucher-linked individual carrying the Chapter 3 phenotype/cytotype package
hole_classes.claim: converts a single public species tip into a two-representative public-plus-own species unit

hole_classes.new_individuals_per_species: 1-2 additional only after first nationwide tree
hole_classes.placement: widespread, non-monophyletic, polyploid, hybrid-suspected, or strongly discordant taxa only
hole_classes.claim: network and species-boundary sensitivity, not baseline coverage

formula.symbols: N=final admitted Japanese species count; M=38 Moreyra Japanese concepts; R=number of Moreyra concepts requiring two-new-sample repair

geographic_hole_priority.why: island endemics or isolated lineages can occupy long or otherwise unsampled branches and should not wait behind redundant mainland duplicates
geographic_hole_priority.sample_rule: two representatives per admitted species; use different islands when the species spans islands, otherwise separated localities away from obvious hybrid zones

geographic_hole_priority.why: the northern Japanese radiation is much richer than the current 38-tip representation
geographic_hole_priority.sample_rule: two populations/occurrences per species where feasible

geographic_hole_priority.why: short-range alpine lineages are easily omitted and may break long apparent branches in the sparse backbone
geographic_hole_priority.sample_rule: two independent occurrences where feasible; one-sample conservation-limited status is preferable to substitution

geographic_hole_priority.why: fills Kinki-Chugoku-Kyushu regional radiations that are sparsely represented by the current public skeleton
geographic_hole_priority.sample_rule: two representatives per admitted species before focal population depth

nested_focal_overlap.JPN_36_Cirsium_sieboldii: its two Level-1 repair individuals are drawn from the RAD population bank; no separate tree-only plants
nested_focal_overlap.JPN_06_Cirsium_dipsacolepis: the one new Chapter-3 trait-linked tree representative is drawn from the RAD population bank
nested_focal_overlap.JPN_15_Cirsium_lineare: the one new Chapter-3 trait-linked tree representative is drawn from the RAD population bank
nested_focal_overlap.Cirsium_brevicaule: the two Level-1 missing-tip representatives are one from each M01 discovery population
nested_focal_overlap.Cirsium_irumtiense: the two Level-1 missing-tip representatives are one from each M01 discovery population

field_decision_rule: when choosing between a new taxon that fills H1/H2 and extra depth in an already represented taxon, fill H1/H2 first unless the extra sample is required by a predeclared focal RAD/RNA protocol being executed on the same visit
